source.citation: "South Water Street." Chicagology. Reprinting the early-streets passage of A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, Volume I (1884), with Chicago Illustrated (August 1866) by James W. Sheahan and later Chicago Chronicle (1895) and Chicago Tribune (1895) produce-market articles.
what_it_does_not_supply: any independent corroboration of the Andreas text it shares verbatim with chicagology_prefire233
the claim that South Water was the town's first street
any 1835 description of the street's surface, crown or profile
the mired wagons and drays as an 1835 observation - that passage is explicitly 1848
what_it_supplies: the August 1833 order to pitch South Water Street from the United States Reservation to Randolph Street by April 1834
the July 1834 order to graduate South Water Street so water flowed from each cross street into the river
South Water and Lake as the two principal thoroughfares, early turnpiked and graded
plank sluices across Clark Street draining to the South Branch
the leading thoroughfares turnpiked by the winter of 1836
that town street work stopped at the United States Reservation boundary
